summary.text: Roger Hanshaw is a Republican member of the West Virginia House of Delegates for District 62, where he has served since 2015, and is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election. An attorney with a doctorate in organic chemistry, he became Speaker of the House in August 2018.

paragraphs.text: Roger Hanshaw was born in Charleston, West Virginia, in 1980.

He earned a bachelor's degree in biochemistry from West Virginia University in 2002, a Ph.D. in organic chemistry from the University of Notre Dame in 2006, and a J.D. from the West Virginia University College of Law in 2012.

His career experience includes working as an attorney at Bowles Rice LLP, as chief of staff and general counsel to State Senate Minority Leader Mike Hall, as associate director of the WVU Extension Service, and as a special assistant to the commissioner at the West Virginia Department of Agriculture.
Hanshaw has served in the House of Delegates since 2015 and became speaker of the House on August 29, 2018.
